## Status

**Draft.** Nothing here is fixed until v1.0. Open questions are marked `[?]` inline where they sit, and collected in §11.

::: {.callout-important}

This protocol assumes **snap-trapping**, two trap-nights per group, ~150 individuals, and no live recapture. If any of that changes, the spatial design in §2 and the data capture in §8 need revisiting.

:::

## 1. Purpose and scope

Collect host and paired environmental samples from bank voles (*Clethrionomys glareolus*) at Pallasjärvi, Finnish Lapland, to support WP1 of the Microbial Sensor project: establishing whether structured components of the gut microbiome track host connectivity, using within-campaign spatial co-occurrence as the connectivity proxy. See `data-management-plan.qmd` §2 for how "connected" is operationally defined here, now that this is prospective rather than archived data.

WP1 is Pallasjärvi only: a single prospective field campaign, snap-trapped 12–17 September 2026 `[?]` on Prof. Heikki Henttonen's (LUKE) existing long-term monitoring design, targeting ~150 individuals. There is no archived-sample component.

Sample types: gut tissue (caecum and distal colon, separately), blood or tissue for PUUV serology, soil at capture points, nest and burrow material, field blanks, and off-grid reference soil.

## 2. Site and trapping design

- Field lead: Prof. Heikki Henttonen (LUKE) and team.
- Site: Pallasjärvi long-term monitoring grids.
- 30 small quadrats (SQ), 15 × 15 m, in groups of 3–7, ≥50 m apart within a group.
- Groups in old forest and in peatland/bog; some peatland groups sit near forest, so voles are caught there too.
- Traps set day 1; checked day 2; checked and collected day 3.

This gives four nested spatial scales — capture point, SQ, group, habitat — with gaps between them. The forest/peatland contrast provides a within-site environmental contrast.

The protocol will be updated with Henttonen's full sampling design once it is available.

## 3. Approvals

Biosecurity approval for transporting biological material Uppsala ↔ Finland is handled via the UU biosecurity officer under UU's overarching licence; form drafted and updated 07 Sep 2026. Trapping and animal handling are covered by Henttonen's Finnish permits.

Carry a copy of the approved form with the samples in the car.

## 5. Sample collection

| Sample | Collected by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Blood/tissue for PUUV serology | Henttonen's team, existing SOP | Hantavirus surveillance — unchanged from current practice |
| Caecum | Henttonen's team, at dissection | Host gut community; separate sample ID |
| Distal colon | Henttonen's team, at dissection | Host gut community, standardised against WP2 faecal swabs; separate sample ID |
| Soil at capture point | Field team | Environmental channel |
| Nest/burrow material | Field team with Henttonen's team, opportunistic | Environmental channel — shared-infrastructure signal |
| Field blanks, off-grid reference soil | Field team | Contamination check and biological comparator (§5.5) |

### 5.1 Gut

- Caecum and distal colon in separate bags, one row per animal, two sample IDs.
- Collected by Henttonen's team into minigrip bags at dissection; frozen the same day.
- Transfer from bags to cryovials happens in Uppsala, on dry ice (§10).

Record if the caecum tears during dissection; cross-contamination between caecum and colon breaks the comparison between them.

### 5.2 PUUV serology

Collected and processed by Henttonen's team under their existing SOP, unchanged from current practice. This protocol points to that SOP rather than duplicating it.

`[?]` SOP reference or citation, and confirmation of what "processes the blood" means in practice (serum for ELISA vs. whole blood).

### 5.3 Soil

- Collect at every capture point (~150). Collection is cheap; only a subset will be processed (§5.6).
- Sampling horizon: organic layer beneath the litter, standardised across all points.
- Fill the 2 ml tube to about two-thirds — roughly 0.5–1.5 g depending on how loose the organic layer is. That is two to five extractions' worth, which leaves room for re-extraction. Leave headroom for freeze expansion.
- Clear the litter with a fresh spatula or gloved hand, then scoop directly with the tube mouth or load with a narrow spatula. Nothing that has touched litter goes into the tube.
- One tube per point. Do not take duplicates as routine; a second tube means a second sample ID and is almost never processed.
- New spatula per point. New gloves per point, or between points where practical.
- Record sampling depth (cm below litter) and rough moisture class.

### 5.4 Nest and burrow material

- Opportunistic — collected by both our team and Henttonen's team when encountered, not systematically.
- Must be linked to SQ number.
- Record material type: actual nest / burrow lining / runway debris. These are microbiologically different things.
- Goes into a larger tube or a minigrip bag, not a 2 ml tube. Fibrous material does not compact into a small tube without handling it more than is wise.

### 5.5 Controls collected alongside real samples

- **Field blanks** — an empty tube of the same type, opened at the sampling point, left open for roughly the time a real sample takes, closed, and then handled identically to real samples all the way through extraction and sequencing. These catch airborne and handling contamination. One per group per day, distributed across groups and days rather than collected in one batch.
- **Off-grid reference soil** — background regional soil signature, collected away from any grid or burrow: four off-grid forest and four off-grid peatland (8 total). This is a biological comparator, not a contamination check.

Kit blanks, PCR no-template controls, and the mock community standard are lab-stage controls, not field-collected — see `pilot-lab-protocol.qmd`.

### 5.6 Processing subset (soil)

Collect all ~150; extract and sequence ~55–60:

- One soil per SQ (30)
- Four capture-point soils in each of 5 multi-capture SQs (20) — estimates within-SQ variance and answers whether capture-point resolution is needed
- Four off-grid forest + four off-grid peatland reference soils (8)
- Balanced across forest and peatland

## 6. Field hygiene

- Sterile or single-use dissection tools per individual for gut and nest/burrow sampling specifically. Shared tools across a necropsy series will homogenise the community signal across individuals in a way that is very hard to detect after the fact.
- New spatula per soil point; new gloves per point, or between points where practical.

## 7. Labelling

- Sample ID plus human-readable location on the tube itself.
- Solvent-proof marker.

## 8. Data capture (KoBo)

Three separate forms plus blanks. Location fields identical across all forms — that is the join key.

**Shared location block:** date, group ID, SQ ID, capture point ID, habitat (old forest / peatland), collector initials.

**Form 1 — Voles** (one row per animal): Henttonen's animal ID (**required** — joins to his morphometrics), caecum sample ID, distal colon sample ID, time of trap check, time of dissection, gut fullness (full/partial/empty), caecum torn (y/n), dissector initials, notes.

**Form 2 — Soil:** sample ID, sampling depth, moisture class, position (within quadrat / quadrat edge / off-grid reference), notes.

**Form 3 — Nest/burrow:** sample ID, material type, notes.

**Blanks:** own form or a sample-type field; same location block. Captured in data, not remembered.

Time of check and time of dissection are separate fields. The gap between them is the post-mortem interval covariate — free to record now, unrecoverable later, and the first thing that stops being recorded when the campaign gets busy.

Sample IDs follow the naming scheme in `data-management-plan.qmd`.

## 9. Cold chain

- Samples go to the **field station freezer** during the day.
- Transfer to the **car freezer** (compressor, −18/−20 °C, 18 L) in one batch in the evening. Batch the loading: one door opening per day, not thirty.
- Day's tubes sit in a cool bag while working.
- **Frozen gel packs** in the freezer for thermal mass — this is the real buffer against a power interruption.
- **Min/max logger inside the freezer.**
- Freezer on 12 V while driving, on mains at the station and at overnight stops. Bring the mains adapter.
- No preservative. Samples are stored dry and frozen. This is only defensible while the cold chain holds — hence the logger.

## 10. On arrival in Uppsala

- Transfer gut from minigrip bags to cryovials on dry ice, without thawing.
- Move everything to institutional −20 °C at IEG. Freezer space is confirmed and −20 °C agreed as adequate for soil, nest and gut (Elin, 09 Sep 2026). The gut transfer to cryovials can be scheduled later, before processing.
